info.name: Accusharp HRMS - Full Walkthrough
info.description:
One complete payroll cycle for one employee (EMP005, Priya Kulkarni, September 2026).

RUN THE FOLDERS IN ORDER 00 -> 08. Between folder 02 and 03 you must load the punch SQL into device_logs - there is no API for punches.

Set the `baseUrl` variable if the app is not on http://localhost:8080.

Only POST/PUT/PATCH need a header, and only ever `Content-Type: application/json`. There is no authentication.

item.name: 00 - Look around
item.description: Read-only. Note the ids you get back - you need them when creating an employee.

request.description: The salary breakup is calculated when an employee is saved. Change these percentages before adding people, not after.
HR001=HR, SUP001=SUPERVISOR, EMP001/EMP002=EMPLOYEE.

item.name: 01 - Set up master data
item.description: Create the designation, the employee and the month's holiday.

request.description: Note the returned id - pass it as designationId next.

userId MUST equal the biometric device's user_id.
You send 4 money fields; basicDA / hra / conveyance / education / grossSalaryWage come back derived and cannot be sent.
Mandatory holidays are removed from working days so they can never become LOP.

item.name: 02 - Roster the month
item.description: Without this there are no expected working days and the whole month becomes LOP.

item.name: Bulk assign MORNING shift, Sundays off

request.description: Returns 29 rows: 30 days - 1 holiday. Four of them are flagged weekOff. Leaves 25 working days.

item.name: 03 - Attendance BEFORE leave
item.description: Run the punch SQL first! See docs/testing/device_logs_EMP005_2026-09.sql

request.description:
Expect workingDays 25, presentDays 22, absentDays 3, lopDays 3, overtimeHours 3.5, invalidPunches 0.
All three absences are unpaid right now because the leave is not approved yet.
The 17th shows 11.5 worked hours and 3.5 overtime.

item.name: 04 - Leave workflow
item.description: Employee applies -> supervisor endorses -> HR approves. Only the last step moves balance.

request.description: Quotas are seeded on first read: casual 12, sick 8.
Saves the returned id into the leaveId variable for the next two requests.
Status becomes SUPERVISOR_APPROVED. Balance has NOT moved yet.
Only HR or ADMIN may do this. THIS is the step that consumes balance and offsets LOP.

item.name: 05 - Attendance AFTER approval
item.description: The same call as folder 03 - watch LOP fall from 3 to 1.

request.description: leaveDays is now 2 and lopDays is 1 - only the 29th, where no leave was applied for.

item.name: 06 - Generate & correct attendance
item.description:
Attendance is a stored, reviewable artifact - not a view recomputed on every read.

  generate -> review -> correct -> pay

Two rules make corrections stick: a regeneration preserves MANUAL rows unless you explicitly ask it not to, and a read never writes. Payroll refuses to run until the period has been generated.

Steps 5-9 need docs/testing/device_logs_EMP005_missing_out_punch.sql - run it where the folder says so.

request.description: Nothing has been generated yet, so this is a transient preview computed from raw punches. Crucially it persists nothing - a read can never overwrite a correction.
Writes one emp_daily_attendance row per rostered day. 29 rows: 30 days minus the holiday on the 14th, which was never rostered. Omit userIds to run the whole company.
recordStatus says where each row came from, locked whether payroll has frozen it. A UI badge is: locked ? 'LOCKED' : recordStatus.

item.name: 4. Monthly now reads the stored rows

request.description: Same figures as the preview in step 1, but now sourced from the stored days rather than recomputed from punches.

item.name: 5. RUN THE SQL FIRST - regenerate to pick up the device change

request.description:
Run docs/testing/device_logs_EMP005_missing_out_punch.sql now - it deletes the exit punch on the 25th, the way a real device drops one.

Rerunning generation is safe and is how late-arriving or corrected device data gets picked up. The 25th now has a single punch, so it becomes INVALID_PUNCH and a day actually worked turns into loss of pay. That is the bug this folder exists to fix.
One punch in, none out. status INVALID_PUNCH, invalidPunch true, and the day is worth nothing towards pay.

Supply the exit the device missed. The times are run back through the same calculation service a device punch takes, so a hand-fixed day cannot obey different rules from a machine-read one: 9 hours punch to punch, less the shift's 1 hour unpaid break, gives 8.00 working hours.

remarks is mandatory - a correction without a reason is not auditable.

item.name: 8. The month picks the correction up

request.description: presentDays back to 22 and lopDays back to 1. LOP and payroll inherit corrections automatically because the summary is now a rollup of the stored days.

item.name: 9. Regenerating does NOT undo the correction

request.description: The load-bearing guarantee. The 25th is MANUAL, so it is preserved and reported as manualPreserved rather than recomputed back into an invalid punch. Send overwriteManual true only when you deliberately want to discard corrections.

item.name: 10. Declare a day that has no punches at all

request.description: The 29th has no punch to correct - the device was down, or the employee worked off-site. There are no times to supply, so the day is declared outright and the hours follow the shift. lopDays drops to 0.
Omitting userIds runs every active employee. Anyone with no roster for the month comes back in employeesWithoutRoster rather than failing the run.

item.name: 07 - Payroll
item.description: Payroll now reads the attendance you generated and reviewed - never a fresh recompute, which would discard corrections. Generating locks the month.

request.description: payableDays 24 (25 working - 1 LOP). netSalary 18936.20.
A period is generated once. Use regenerate to correct it.
Writes revision 2 and marks revision 1 SUPERSEDED - the old figure is never overwritten.
rev 2 GENERATED net 19086.20, rev 1 SUPERSEDED net 18936.20.
Skips anyone already generated. Uses zero for all manual deductions.
Generating payroll froze the month so the slip stays reproducible. recordStatus still shows which days a human corrected - locking does not erase that.

item.name: Unlock the month to correct it

request.description: Reopens a paid month. The payroll already generated is untouched - regenerate it afterwards to pick the corrections up.
Any correction after payroll has run needs unlock, fix, regenerate - in that order.

item.name: Regenerate payroll on the corrected attendance

request.description: Supersedes the previous revision rather than editing it, and re-locks the month. The old slip stays reproducible exactly as printed.
Open in a browser and print or save as PDF.

item.name: 09 - Error cases worth seeing
item.description: Every failure returns the same ApiError shape.

request.description: Every field failure is listed in one message.
'Supervisor SUP001 does not manage employee HR001'
Final approval needs the HR or ADMIN role.
An open or approved leave already covers part of this range.
January was never generated, so payroll refuses rather than quietly recomputing from raw punches. This is the guard that stops anyone being paid off numbers nobody reviewed.

exec: pm.test('says to generate first', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('Attendance has not been generated'));

request.description: Run this while the month is locked by payroll. Unlock it first.

item.name: 400 - an employee cannot correct their own attendance

request.description: Correcting attendance moves money, so it is restricted to HR and ADMIN.

item.name: 400 - a correction with nothing to apply

request.description: Give punch times or a status. Neither is not a correction.

item.name: 404 - correcting a day that was never generated

request.description: You can only correct attendance that exists - generate the month first.
